term: selected function and local biological advantage
definition: A selected-function explanation appeals to a heritable trait’s differential survival or reproductive contribution in a specified environment, not its anticipation of a future end. In the stipulated Boolean filter a variant persists exactly when present, heritable and advantageous. The filter is a deterministic special case; Darwin’s tendency to preservation does not assert this rule for every actual organism. Neutral variants, drift, changing environments and historical contingency prevent inference of global optimality.
note: Stipulated finite test of mechanism and agency independence, informed by the separate Darwin and Blount occurrence claims. A population-genetic model would require further sourced equations.
